extraction.name: TravelPlanner
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating language agents in real-world travel planning with multiple constraints and tool use. It provides a static sandbox environment with around four million data entries accessible via tools, and 1,225 curated travel queries with reference plans.
extraction.creator: Jian Xie; Kai Zhang; Jiangjie Chen; Tinghui Zhu; Renze Lou; Yuandong Tian; Yanghua Xiao; Yu Su
extraction.citeAs: Xie, Jian, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, and Yu Su. TravelPlanner: A Benchmark for Real-World Planning with Language Agents. arXiv:2402.01622v4, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was constructed through: (1) environment and evaluation setup, (2) diverse travel query design, (3) reference plan annotation, and (4) quality check. The environment is a static and closed sandbox for consistent and unbiased evaluations. Queries were synthesized from fundamental elements including departure city, destination, date range, travel duration, and hard constraints, then GPT-4 was used to generate natural language queries. To ensure every query had at least one feasible plan, 20 graduate students annotated plans for synthesized queries, resulting in 1,225 validated query-plan pairs. The authors then reviewed every query and plan and recalibrated each query's budget using costs from corresponding human-annotated plans.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The sandbox environment contains data for CitySearch, FlightSearch, DistanceMatrix, RestaurantSearch, AttractionSearch, and AccommodationSearch. Original data sources are publicly available Internet data, including the Kaggle Flight Status Prediction dataset for flights, Google Distance Matrix API for driving distance and time, the Kaggle Zomato Restaurants Dataset for restaurants, Google Places API for attractions, and the Kaggle Airbnb Open Data Dataset for accommodations. The paper states the data were then modified by adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values to suit requirements.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Flight data were extracted from 2022-03-01 to 2022-04-01. Travel queries in the benchmark use dates in March 2022, and the sandbox data are based on 2022.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors modified sourced data by adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values to suit benchmark requirements and avoid data contamination. For FlightSearch, they retained selected fields and generated Price by multiplying Distance by a random factor from 0.2 to 0.5. For DistanceMatrix, they computed Price by multiplying Distance by 1 for self-driving and 0.15 for taxi, then stored results in the database. For RestaurantSearch, they extracted restaurant name and average cost, randomly assigned restaurants to cities, and randomly categorized cuisines. For AttractionSearch, they retained selected fields and stored API results in the database. For AccommodationSearch, they extracted key details, randomly assigned items to cities, and randomly assigned room rules.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: To create diverse queries, the authors randomly chose departure city, destination, and date range to form query skeletons, then adjusted travel duration and number of hard constraints to create different complexity levels. They used GPT-4 to generate natural language queries from these elements. The authors also recalibrated each query's budget using costs from corresponding human-annotated plans instead of initial heuristic-generated budgets. For evaluation, key components from natural language plans were extracted and reconstructed into a formally structured plan using GPT-4-Turbo before automatic script-based evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Twenty graduate students were invited to meticulously annotate plans for synthesized queries. One plan was deemed eligible only if it met all constraints outlined in the evaluation script. This process produced 1,225 validated query-plan pairs. The authors additionally performed detailed review of every query and plan and rectified errors found. The paper also notes that the training set includes 45 queries with human-annotated plans.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A plan was accepted only if it satisfied all constraints in the evaluation script. Through multiple stages of human verification, the authors ensured high quality and the presence of at least one feasible solution for each query. For evaluation of model outputs, key components were extracted from natural language plans and organized into structured plans for automatic evaluation.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 for generating natural language queries; GPT-4-Turbo for extracting key components from natural language plans into structured format
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state that they will release evaluation scripts to foster innovation and aid development of new methods. No versioning timeframe, maintainers, or deprecation policy is specified.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: User queries may include number of people and preferences such as bringing pets. The paper discusses user needs and constraints including room rule, room type, cuisine, transportation preference, budget, and presence of children under 10 years old in some examples.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to provide an effective benchmark for complex planning in future research and to serve as a catalyst for future research toward more capable language agents. The authors note that some data are derived from publicly available Internet data and do not represent the authors' viewpoints. They also acknowledge that definitions of commonsense may differ and encourage discussion to enrich the commonsense dimension. They encourage use of evaluation feedback in the training set, but strictly prohibit cheating on validation and test sets to uphold fairness and reliability.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors state that the static and closed sandbox environment is designed for consistent and unbiased evaluations by ensuring all agents access the same unchanging information and avoiding variability and potential biases introduced by dynamic data. They also note that their current commonsense evaluation criteria are based on the authors' consensus and that everyone's definition of commonsense may be different.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark uses a static and closed sandbox rather than dynamic real-world data. Some data are derived from publicly available Internet data and modified for benchmark requirements. The commonsense criteria are based on the authors' consensus, and the authors acknowledge that definitions of commonsense may differ. The paper also states that cheating on validation and test sets is prohibited.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed as a benchmark for evaluating language agents' tool-use and complex planning abilities under multiple constraints. It is divided into training, validation, and test sets. The training set contains 45 queries with human-annotated plans, the validation set contains 180 queries, and the test set contains 1,000 queries. The authors encourage use of evaluation feedback in the training set, such as reinforcement learning techniques, but strictly prohibit any form of cheating on the validation and test sets.
